subject: Urban Planning
title: Telecom Infrastructure: The Digital Divide
description: A micro-lesson that makes Telecom Infrastructure: The Digital Divide usable.

hook.text: 42 million Americans lack access to broadband internet. In rural areas, one in four households has no reliable connection.

buildup.text: Internet access is now essential — for school, work, healthcare, and government services. Without it, you're excluded.

discovery.text: South Korea invested heavily in fiber optic networks in the 2000s. Now 99% of Koreans have gigabit broadband at low cost.

twist.text: US telecom companies received $400 billion in subsidies to build rural broadband. Much of it was never built.

climax.text: Municipal broadband — city-owned internet — offers faster, cheaper service, but telecom lobbying has banned it in 18 states.

punchline.text: The internet is a utility. We just refuse to treat it like one.

quiz.question: Why has rural broadband expansion failed in the US despite massive subsidies?
options: Rural areas don't have enough demand to justify broadband investment
Telecom companies received billions in subsidies but didn't build the infrastructure
Federal regulations prevent broadband installation in agricultural zones
